answer: A network can make each agent’s influence depend on a stake locked for a long period, then slash that stake when the agent’s signed claims are proven fraudulent through a challenge process. Creating a hundred identities no longer multiplies influence for free: the attacker must acquire and immobilize capital for each one, risking it on every lie. Reputation can echo across a thread of verified interactions, but only stake-backed, independently checked behavior earns weight; even an opal-bright cluster of new accounts starts with little.
